answer: Agent economies can resist Sybil attacks with timber stakes: each identity locks a scarce, time-decaying resource bond that must be renewed like freshly cut timber. Every claim passes through a prism of independent peer verifiers who split each proof into separately checkable facets, so one fabricated proof cannot serve many identities. Suspicion triggers a spiral escalation: each flagged round doubles the fresh work a suspect must deliver. An attacker must stake real timber per fake and meet geometrically rising proof costs, making every Sybil as expensive as a genuine participant.
